Try /r/fakeapp and look for criteria for good image selection to create training material for the target face. Basically you want pictures that are good quality (not pixeled, blurred, hair or hands in face,..) and all different angles (frontal, head up, down, to the side, and all combos), face expressions and different light situations, the app struggles with profile pics so you don't need many or any of those.

High quality videos (for example interviews on youtube) are a good source to get a large number of pictures fast.

I'd say 1k-2k pics that cover the criteria are more than enough, better than 5k pics of bad quality. The app will mirror and rotate them in training anyways to create more input data.

At the end, all you need to upload is the extracted faces of those images. They'll be 256x256 and created by the alignment script that detects faces in pictures (for run of the alignment the source pictures need to be the same type, e.g. png or jpg)

Quick guide what I did to create facesets:

  • I used fakeapp v1.1, it can Extract from images and not videos only with no fps input option like v2.1

  • collect a images from photoshoots etc (jpgs mostly, convert non jpgs to jpg), put them in one folder. Optional: cut out faces manually and overwrite the file, produces smaller images with the same desired target and makes the job easier for the alignment (esp. with multiple faces in a picture). Select your image folder and run Extract using the CPU (GPU can't handle larger input images). This will create a folder "aligned" in the folder that contains extracted face. Delete any bad results, mis-crops, wrong faces (multiple faces in source image). We only want good clear faces for training.

  • For videos as source, I used HD interviews from youtube (download them with the tool of your choice, I used jdownloader). Look for videos that match our criteria for good source. 5-10 or even more different videos will be better than just one or 2.

  • Get frames from videos: ffmpeg -i <videofile> -vf fps=<framerate> "<outputfilename%d.png>" (get the latest version of ffmpeg, add it's path to the windows path environment variable)

  • Use frame rates depending on length and head movement speed of the video. 1 (default) up to 5 fps is more than enough. We don't want too many duplicates.

  • I created one folder per video, put the video in there, opened the command line for that folder (click into explorer address bad, type "cmd" and hit enter) and ran ffmpeg for each folder.

  • Before running Extract for the folder, go through the frames and delete all bad frames (not the face we want or mostly blurred or unclear).

  • Run Extract on the CPU for each video folder (input type png now).

  • Tip: You can run multiple Extract jobs in parallel, just open additional instances of fakeapp. I ran up to 4 on my laptop, but also had training running. It saves A LOT of time.

  • Finally, copy all the great aligned images you have created into one single folder, make an archive, upload and share and you're done :)
